chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad and others, from Sahl ibn Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group from our companions who gather and prayer time arrives, and one says to another, 'Step forward, so-and-so.' He said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The people should be led in prayer by the best reciter of the Quran. If they are equal in recitation, then the one who migrated earlier (in Hijrah). If they are equal in Hijrah, then the eldest in age. If they are equal in age, then let the one most knowledgeable of the Sunnah and most learned in religion lead them. And let none of you step forward over a man in his own house, nor a master of authority over his own authority.' And when you pray behind one whom you follow, it is not permissible for you to recite behind him for the rest of the prayer, whether it is a prayer where recitation is pronounced aloud or one where it is not. You must glorify Allah (Exalted) and declare His oneness, unless it is a prayer where recitation is pronounced aloud and you do not hear it, for then it is obligatory upon you to recite. And if you hear part of the recitation, it suffices you, even if some of it is hidden from you. And that which indicates what we mentioned is what was narrated:

key_terms.اَلْهِجْرَةِ: Migration (from Mecca to Medina, used as a merit metric)

ai.seo_question: Who should lead the prayer if companions are equal in Quran recitation, and when must a follower recite behind the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the primary criteria for Imam selection, emphasizing Quranic proficiency as the foremost merit, a principle central to Shia jurisprudence for ensuring liturgical accuracy. It further clarifies the follower's obligation to remain silent and listen during the Imam's recitation, except in loud prayers where auditory separation necessitates independent recitation, reflecting the scholarly distinction between *Jahr* and *Ikhfa*.
